decision: Rejected: direct arithmetic projection saves only 0.10% / 0.072% of whole-build instructions. Keep one established projection path instead of adding a context-readiness traversal for negligible measured benefit. No timing gate or full suite was spent on the rejected experiment.
patch:
diff --git a/core/compiler/dewy_fast.jo b/core/compiler/dewy_fast.jo
index 97f913d5..dcc2c569 100644
--- a/core/compiler/dewy_fast.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/dewy_fast.jo
@@ -342,7 +342,34 @@ dn_op_node = (kind: DewyKind, symbol: DewyToken, offset: int, children: int[]) -
     dewy_syntax.push(DewySyntax(kind, "", mkpos(dn_file, offset), children, symbol))
     id
 
+# An arithmetic operand has value syntax. Project complete simple operands
+# once while parsing, instead of allocating another syntax-child buffer and
+# walking the same arithmetic tree again. Contextual `end` remains deferred
+# until the enclosing index establishes its axis.
+dn_value_ready = (id: int) -> bool:
+    k = dewy_syntax[id].kind
+    if k == .core_expr or k == .source_integer or k == .source_real or k == .boolean or k == .string: return true
+    if k == .identifier: return dewy_syntax[id].text != "end"
+    if k == .block and dewy_syntax[id].text == "():" and dewy_syntax[id].children.len() == 1: return dn_value_ready(dw_child(id, 0))
+    if k != .binary: return false
+    op = dewy_syntax[id].symbol
+    if op == .dot: return dn_value_ready(dw_child(id, 1)) and dewy_syntax[dw_child(id, 2)].kind == .identifier
+    if op != .call: return false
+    if not dn_value_ready(dw_child(id, 1)): return false
+    args = dw_child(id, 2)
+    if dewy_syntax[args].kind != .block or dewy_syntax[args].text != "():": return false
+    loop arg in dewy_syntax[args].children:
+        if not dn_value_ready(arg): return false
+    true
+
 dn_operator = (kind: DewyKind, op: DewyToken, left: int, right: int) -> int:
+    if kind == .binary and (op == .plus or op == .minus or op == .star) and dn_value_ready(left) and dn_value_ready(right):
+        pos = dewy_syntax[left].pos
+        n = mk(.binary, pos)
+        nodes[n].op = i32(int(if op == .plus: Tok.plus else if op == .minus: Tok.minus else: Tok.star))
+        nodes[n].a = i32(dw_expr(left))
+        nodes[n].b = i32(dw_expr(right))
+        return dn_node(.core_expr, "", pos_off(pos), name = i32(n))
     scalar = dn_token_uninvert(op)
     sentinel = if scalar != op: 1 else: 0
     dn_op_node(kind, scalar, pos_off(dewy_syntax[left].pos), [sentinel, left, right])
diff --git a/core/compiler/dewy_parse.jo b/core/compiler/dewy_parse.jo
index 71a24485..a94b59fb 100644
--- a/core/compiler/dewy_parse.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/dewy_parse.jo
@@ -15,7 +15,7 @@ enum DewyKind:
     unknown, op, identifier, boolean, metatag, based_string, integer, real,
     quoted, rawquoted, eof, atom, ambiguous, binary, block, combined_assignment,
     flat, flow, interpolated_string, inverted_comparison, keyword, keyword_expr,
-    operator, postfix, prefix, string, string_chunk, source_integer, source_real
+    operator, postfix, prefix, string, string_chunk, source_integer, source_real, core_expr
 
 dw_kind_name = (kind: DewyKind) -> str:
     match kind:
@@ -48,6 +48,7 @@ dw_kind_name = (kind: DewyKind) -> str:
         prefix: "Prefix"
         string: "String"
         string_chunk: "StringChunk"
+        core_expr: "Expression"
 
 dw_kind_from_name = (name: str) -> DewyKind:
     match name:
@@ -593,6 +594,7 @@ dw_broadcast = (op: DewyToken, a: int, b: int, id: int) -> int:
 dw_expr = (id: int) -> int:
     let id = dw_unwrap(id)
     k = dewy_syntax[id].kind
+    if k == .core_expr: return int(dewy_syntax[id].name)
     text = dewy_syntax[id].text
     pos = dewy_syntax[id].pos
     if k == .based_string: return dw_binary(id)
limits: Hardware instruction counts are not timings. This experiment does not rule out a broader frontend redesign.
